slot_why: One Reel a week. Both family-pressure winners went out in the 08:00 slot (JR-0060 'when is it your turn' at a wedding, 12.9K Instagram views, Sat 2026-10-31 08:00; JR-0071 relatives asking salary questions, 5.4K, Tue 2026-10-27 08:00). Monday 08:00 is the first slot of each plan week, so the lane never displaces an episode already in Buffer. Instagram slot times are unchanged; the same video also goes to YouTube in its MORNING slot (coordination same_slot).
rules: Every episode follows R1-R13. The verse is quoted verbatim from the KJV and must mean in its own passage what the episode uses it for (R10). No other-faith festival framing (R5): weddings, family lunches, baby showers and phone calls stay; pujas and festival tables do not. Jesus never gives financial, medical or legal advice and never promises an outcome (a reconciliation, a child, a match).
source: content-os/community/ideas.md, '2026-11-04 family-pressure lane' (commit fed5f77), six ideas with context-checked verses

backlog.idea: Refused a match whose family wanted her to quit her job; her mother hasn't spoken to her in 4 days.
backlog.r10_context: Psalm 27 is David's confidence in the LORD when surrounded and abandoned; v10: even if father and mother forsake me, the LORD will take me up. Used for: a parent's silence is not the last word on whether you are held. Not used to call the mother wicked or to cut her off.

backlog.idea: Aunty at the wedding says 'you've put on weight' in front of everyone; she laughs it off and stops eating.
backlog.r10_context: 1 Samuel 16:6-13: the LORD tells Samuel not to judge Jesse's sons by appearance or height when choosing a king; the LORD looks on the heart. Used for: how God sees her is not how the table sees her. Not used to dismiss health.

backlog.idea: Grandmother asks to see a great-grandchild 'before I go'; he smiles and changes the subject.
backlog.r10_context: Ecclesiastes 3:1-8: God has appointed times for every matter under heaven. Used for: his life's timing is not a race set by the family's clock. Not a promise that marriage or a child will come.

backlog.idea: Finds her father's loan papers for her wedding; he says 'don't worry about it'.
backlog.r10_context: Psalm 103:8-14: the LORD's compassion is like a father's pity for his children; He knows our frame. Used for: a father's quiet sacrifice is a picture of the Father's compassion. Jesus gives no financial advice about the loan.

backlog.idea: The earning son abroad is asked again to fund his brother's house; he sends it and eats Maggi for the month.
backlog.r10_context: Galatians 6:1-5: each one tests his own work and carries his own load, alongside 6:2 'bear ye one another's burdens'. Used for: love helps carry a brother's burden, but he is not meant to carry the whole house alone. Balance with 6:2; Jesus gives no money advice (the lint flags it).

backlog.idea: At a baby shower a relative whispers that God is punishing the childless couple.
backlog.r10_context: John 9:1-7: the disciples assume the man's blindness is punishment for sin; Jesus says neither he nor his parents sinned. Used for: their childlessness is not God's punishment. Never promise a child (the lint flags promised outcomes).
